mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong earnings growth (INDPRO > 0.5% monthly).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or during periods when labor market indicators (UNRATE, PAYEMS) are strengthening.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.4 percentage points, coinciding with a stagnation in payroll employment (PAYEMS), signals labor market imbalances that precede cyclical corrections and negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with wage inflation concerns
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered events, or the mechanism fails when consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below -0.3% for three consecutive months signals a broad-based supply shock, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or during periods of strong demand growth (GDPC1 > 0.5% quarterly).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and mortgage interest rates (implied via HOUST price declines) signals restrictive credit conditions, which depresss housing and business investment and result in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises >0.25% AND HOUST falls >2% monthly
regime_hint: monetary tightening with housing market sensitivity
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or during periods of robust consumer spending growth (GDPC1 > 0.4% quarterly).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS rising while GDPC1 grows slowly) signals elevated precautionary behavior by households, which reduces near-term consumption and corporate revenue, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or when labor market indicators (UNRATE, PAYEMS) are rapidly improving.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for two consecutive months, accompanied by a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS), signals a deepening labor market downturn that reduces consumer purchasing power and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6.5% for 2 consecutive months AND PAYEMS falls
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or during periods of strong inflationary pressure (CPIAUCSL > 0.4% monthly).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.4% for three consecutive months, with stagnant real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), signals rising inflation with weak demand, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 0.4% for 3 consecutive months AND GDPC1 flat
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or when monetary policy is aggressively tightening (FEDFUNDS > 1.5% monthly).
